jobs.title: Vice President Finance
jobs.description:
About the Company

Our client is a multi-company industrial services group specializing in mechanical related services. They are looking for a VP Finance who will be responsible for
people leadership, process improvement, and change management. They will lead budgeting, forecasting, cash flow management, KPI reporting, and financial performance analysis.

Why Work Here

Potential career path toward Head of Finance for Canada.
Growing organization with an active acquisition pipeline and opportunities to participate in M&A integration.
Meaningful ownership of finance across multiple operating businesses.
Opportunity to improve processes, strengthen controls and build a high-performing finance team.

About the Opportunity

Key responsibilities:
50% — People leadership, process improvement and change management: Develop and train finance staff, improve local processes and controls, strengthen operational workflows and ensure consistent financial practices across the businesses. Work closely with Operations to address process gaps and improve accountability.
20% — FP&A: Lead budgeting, forecasting, cash flow management, KPI reporting and financial performance analysis.
30% — Strategic leadership: Partner with the President as a finance thought partner, support business decisions, challenge assumptions where appropriate and contribute to growth and M&A integration.
This is a hands-on position, not a purely strategic or oversight role. The individual must understand the underlying transactions and financial details and be prepared to assist with month-end close or other accounting activities when required.

First 6–12 months:
Learn the individual businesses, the company's reporting cadence and KPIs.
Understand local operations, revenue recognition, project accounting, the P&L and balance sheet.
Assess existing financial processes, controls and reporting, then establish a roadmap for improvements.
Develop the finance team and improve collaboration with Operations.
Make a meaningful impact on the business and become a trusted thought partner to the President.
Support the onboarding and integration of an acquired business into the group.

About You

Current title: VP Finance or CFO
Overall 10+ experience with change management, process improvement, reporting, FP&A and leadership
Experience in a business with revenues under $100M preferred
Industry backgrounds: construction, engineering, manufacturing, HVAC, industrial services or other project-based businesses.
M&A exposure
Comfortable adopting technology and AI tools to improve financial processes.
Experience working across multiple locations, legal entities or decentralized business units.
Experience implementing financial controls, standardizing processes and improving reporting.
Familiarity with ERP improvements, automation, analytics and AI-enabled finance tools.

Salary Range

$200,000 - $220,000 base salary + bonus

Click the “Apply Now” button and follow the instructions to submit your resume. Please know that we only accept documents in MS Word or Rich Text formats.

jobs.description:
Our client is an established integrated lifecycle management company and looking for a Director of Business Decision Support and Financial Performance to join their team. The Director will lead the Business Decision Support & Financial Performance function, providing financial reporting, forecasting, variance analysis, benchmarking, and insights to drive better business decisions and resource allocation. Reporting to the CFO, they will build and lead a high-performing Business Analyst team supporting budgets, forecasts, P&Ls, and performance metrics across the business. The role is highly cross-functional, partnering with Operations and leaders across PMO, Purchasing, IT, and Finance to improve processes, systems, and overall business performance.

Assisting in project planning, controls, and monitoring.
Developing and maintaining models related to cost performance.
Reviewing cost control and financial reporting procedures and recommend changes or improvements as necessary.
Assisting in the preparation of department budget and forecasting, gathering departmental data, assessing the validity, and reporting into appropriate formats.
Responsible for the annual and quarterly target setting process.
Responsible for financial reporting of the department, including multi-entities within the business area.
Providing advice, guidance, recommendations and assistance to line staff and management in assessing projects, reporting, cost benefit analysis, and cost allocation.

Reporting:

Ensure alignment of Pillar based monthly management reporting with key highlights and analysis.
Perform Margins, P&L and Balance Sheet analysis and reviews together with Pillar leads and CFO.
Lead and co-ordinate the monthly variance analysis of financial results and comparisons to annual budgets, forecasts and prior year, along with explanations of key drivers.
Build the narrative that explains the Operational results and plans to the Executive Management team.
Financial tools and dashboard development to support operations.
Support Central Finance team with external reporting requirements and variance explanations.
Lead Cashflow reporting requirements (Treasury) by consolidating inputs from multiple sources (i.e. Tax, AP/AR, etc.).
Backup and support CFO for internal and external reporting requirements.

Business Decision and FP&A Support:

Leads analysis of financial information to support effective business decisions.
Manage and support the Business Analysis team, ensuring business planning and financial forecasting process and the annual budgeting process is consistent across the team and all Finance and Operations deadlines are met.
Support the refinement of the monthly forecasting process, working with the Central Finance teams.
Analyze and interpret operating and financial results to identify trends and activities driving those results and make recommendations on potential changes, both operational and financial in nature, to improve performance.
Provide competitive benchmarking and optimization of company resources including resource allocation decision support.
Adhoc analysis as needed.

Central Finance and Parent Company Support

Promote process improvements that focus on elimination of complex manual processes.
Support finance related projects, e.g., SAP migration, internal and external audit requests, tax strategy planning, transfer pricing, etc.
Cash management planning, providing accrued, deferred revenue forecasts, accounts receivable collection timing as well as accounts payable forecasting in collaboration with Central finance teams.
Ensure adherence and consistency with capital expenditure business case justification and analysis to support investment decisions.
Work closely with counterparts at parent company to establish and promote shared best practices.

What You Need to Succeed

An undergraduate degree/diploma in the appropriate field (business administration, accounting, mathematics) or equivalent.
Requires a CPA designation.
10+ years related experience in business analysis/project analysis.
Advanced Excel, PowerPoint, and Office365 skills.
Experience with SharePoint an asset.
Excellent interpersonal and communications skills and the willingness and ability to lead change in the finance function.
Detailed and focused with strong analytical skills, ability to prepare financial reports for senior leadership team.
Strong organizational and time management skills with a sense of urgency and accountability.
Good understanding of HU (Human Performance) tools to develop an error free culture, based on continuous improvement and self-checking.
Extensive ERP knowledge and experience, with SAP preferred.
Good familiarity with utility and OEM project/industry/technology and understanding of aspects of work programs and projects associated with cost engineering, work planning and project performance analysis.
Demonstrated ability to lead a team of individuals with diverse skill sets aligning them to exceed organizational goals.
Excellent problem-solving skills and high commitment to quality and delivering on client commitments, including experience in leading complex projects to successful conclusions.
Strong team building, decision-making, mentorship, and people management skills.
Innovative, enthusiastic, and ready to be part of our dynamic leadership team.

Detailed Job Description

Job Overview

The Senior Regional Vice President (SRVP) is responsible for leading and managing overall business operations, market development, strategic execution, and organizational management within a designated region, ensuring that regional operational goals align with the company’s overarching strategic direction. This role entails comprehensive oversight of regional business performance, operational management, financial results, market expansion, client relations, and team development. The SRVP drives sustainable growth within the region while ensuring that all business activities comply with company policies, standards, and management requirements.

The SRVP works closely with the CEO, COO, CFO, other regional leaders, and the corporate executive team to formulate regional development strategies, facilitate cross-regional resource coordination, oversee the execution of major business initiatives, and resolve critical operational issues. Furthermore, the SRVP is responsible for cultivating regional management talent, optimizing operational systems, and enhancing market competitiveness to ensure long-term, stable business growth and operational success within the assigned region.

Key Responsibilities

I. Regional Strategic Planning and Leadership

Develop and implement long-term development strategies and annual operational plans for the assigned region, ensuring that regional objectives are aligned with the company’s overall strategy, financial goals, and market development direction. Analyze the regional market environment, industry trends, competitive landscape, and customer needs to identify new business opportunities and potential risks. Establish regional management standards and execution mechanisms, define the responsibilities, objectives, and performance requirements for each business unit, and drive the effective implementation of regional strategies.

II. Regional Business Operations and Performance Management

Provide comprehensive oversight of the daily operations of all business departments, branches, and operational units within the region, ensuring that business processes run efficiently and meet established performance targets. Regularly review revenue performance, operational efficiency, service quality, customer satisfaction, and business growth; identify operational deviations promptly and develop corrective measures. Coordinate activities across different departments within the region to resolve significant issues that impact business execution and operational efficiency.

III. Financial Management and Operational Goal Control

Oversee regional budget development, financial planning, cost control, and the analysis of operational results, ensuring that regional financial objectives align with the company’s overall financial plan. Collaborate with the CFO and the finance team to review regional revenue, profit, operating expenses, cash flow, and return on investment (ROI). Establish mechanisms for monitoring budget execution and financial performance; control operating costs effectively; enhance the efficiency of regional resource utilization; and ensure that all business units achieve their established financial objectives.

IV. Market Expansion and Business Growth

Lead regional market development, business expansion, and commercial growth initiatives, identifying potential customer segments, emerging markets, and strategic partnership opportunities. Oversee the development of sales channels, customer acquisition, marketing campaigns, and business collaborations to drive the growth of regional market share and enhance corporate brand influence. Partner with business development, sales, and marketing teams to formulate market-entry strategies and customer growth plans, ensuring the sustained competitiveness of the regional business.

V. Organizational Management and Team Leadership

Responsible for establishing and refining the regional management structure, and overseeing the performance of regional department heads and senior management. Define team performance objectives, talent development programs, and succession plans for management roles to strengthen regional organizational capabilities and the execution proficiency of the leadership team. Foster a positive corporate culture and cross-departmental collaboration, ensuring that managers at all levels effectively implement company policies, operational goals, and management requirements.

VI. Customer Relations and Strategic Partnership Management

Oversee the management of key regional customer relationships, strategic partnerships, and major commercial contracts, ensuring timely responses to customer needs and the stability of collaborative ties. Participate in negotiations with major clients, business collaborations, and the drafting and review of critical business agreements; coordinate the resolution of significant customer complaints, service disputes, and partnership-related issues. Collaborate with customer success, sales, and operations teams to improve customer satisfaction, retention rates, and long-term partnership value.

Monitor operational, financial, legal, and market risks within regional business activities, and establish effective mechanisms for risk identification, assessment, and mitigation. Ensure that all regional business units comply with applicable laws, industry regulations, internal corporate policies, and regulatory requirements. Work with legal, compliance, finance, and internal audit teams to periodically review regional management processes and internal controls, addressing significant compliance issues promptly and driving the implementation of corrective actions.

VIII. Communication with Senior Management and Strategic Execution

Provide regular reports to the CEO, COO, and the corporate executive management team regarding regional operational performance, market developments, financial results, business risks, and the progress of strategic plan execution. Provide management counsel regarding regional expansion, organizational restructuring, major investments, and business transformation. Facilitate the sharing of resources and information between various regions and corporate headquarters, ensure the unified execution of corporate strategy at the regional level, and drive long-term, sustainable growth for regional operations.

Bachelor’s degree or higher in Business Administration, Management, Marketing, Financial Management, Economics, or a related field.

Prior training in areas such as corporate operations management, strategic planning, financial management, or leadership is an advantage.

Proficiency in corporate management, regional market strategy, budget management, and risk control principles.

Portfolio Leadership

Lead the Organizational Development, Total Rewards, HR Operations and People Analytics portfolio, setting clear priorities, accountabilities and measures of success.
Turn the firm’s people priorities into focused plans and practical outcomes.
Use workforce data, external information and business context to identify risks and opportunities and provide clear recommendations.

Work with HR Business Partners and business leaders to improve the quality and consistency of talent discussions and decisions.
Use talent data and feedback to identify firmwide themes, risks and areas requiring attention.
Clarify roles, accountabilities and ways of working across HR as these practices evolve.

Workforce Insights

Lead the firm’s workforce insights agenda by identifying the workforce questions, trends and risks that matter most to the business.
Work through the People Analytics team to strengthen the quality, relevance and use of workforce reporting and analysis.
Move the function beyond producing standard reports toward providing insights and recommendations that support business, talent and workforce decisions.

Work with Finance, HR Business Partners, Talent Acquisition and other stakeholders to bring together business context, workforce data and external talent-market information.

Ensure reward programs remain competitive, sustainable and aligned with business priorities, market trends and workforce needs.
Oversee the evolution of reward and recognition practices that support attraction, retention and performance.
Advance the firm’s approach to employee wellbeing, ensuring it remains responsive to evolving workforce needs and expectations and supports sustainable performance and a positive employee experience.

HR Operations & Enablement

Set clear priorities for improving HR processes, systems and services, with a focus on simplicity, consistency and the needs of employees, leaders and HR teams.
Sponsor practical opportunities to use technology, automation and AI to reduce manual work and improve service delivery.
Ensure the People Analytics team provides accurate, timely and useful workforce reporting and analysis.
Connect operational, reporting and technology priorities to the broader needs of HR and the business.

The Head of Credit & Portfolio Management is the senior leader of the Portfolio Management (PM) function across Global Corporate Banking in Canada and the U.S. The role owns PM governance, standards and risk oversight. It serves as the senior PM approval authority within the delegated lending framework, leads active portfolio management and credit structuring excellence, and is the principal Corporate Banking representative to Risk, Compliance, Internal Audit and regulators on PM matters.

The role sets the standards and the operating model. Lending Unit PM leaders own business execution, staffing and portfolio outcomes. The role partners with Risk & Financial Management, Capital Markets and Global Transaction Banking, and applies effective challenge within BMO’s Risk Appetite framework.

Key Accountabilities

Governance & Standards
Act as the key governance driver for the PM function; own PM standards, policy interpretation and governance consistency across Corporate Banking.
Maintain a common PM operating playbook across LUs, standardizing intent and repeatable work rather than org models.
Provide Corporate Banking input to BMO corporate policies and lending directives, and ensure policies are interpreted and applied correctly.
Hold a standing seat on credit and risk committees as a delegate to the Co-Heads of Global Corporate Banking, with a documented escalation protocol.
Credit Governance & Approval Authority
Exercise delegated approval authority within delegated limits for transactions above LU PM head authority.
Serve as delegate for Business Head signoffs for the Co-Heads of Global Corporate Banking.
Provide effective challenge on material credit, underwriting and portfolio risk; escalate significant policy, governance or risk concerns.
Represent Corporate Banking on the U.S. Allowance Committee and contribute to the allowance and provisioning outlook.
Ensure risk-taking stays within the Risk Appetite framework, agreed limits and regulatory requirements.
Regulatory, Audit & Control Leadership
Act as the primary PM representative with Risk, Compliance, Internal Audit and regulators; lead on exams and reviews relating to Corporate Banking.
Lead PM-related remediation and regulatory change initiatives; act as direct counterpart to 2nd and 3rd line workstreams.
Ensure control effectiveness and audit readiness, including 1st line quality assurance of credit processes.
Portfolio Monitoring & Risk Insights
Act as chief architect of the KRI dashboard and wider monitoring controls; own a common Corporate Banking PM reporting framework covering KRIs, watchlist migration, EWIs and past dues.
Provide management insight on portfolio trends, concentrations and emerging risks, including sector and macro developments, working with sector heads and Industry Verticals.
Direct oversight of high-risk accounts: risk-rating accuracy, timely action on deteriorating credits, and Special Assets liaison with lessons-learned sessions.
Contribute stress testing and scenario analysis inputs for the Corporate Banking portfolio.
Own the PM data and reporting technology roadmap to establish a common fact base.
Active Portfolio Management & Capital Productivity
Maintain a Corporate Banking de-risking playbook with trigger frameworks for emerging risk and shifting concentrations.
Provide Corporate Banking input to the industry, single-name, tenor and product limit framework, and monitor the portfolio against it.
Partner with Capital Markets on hold levels, distribution, hedging and risk-transfer levers.
Maintain a long-term portfolio view that balances profitable growth with credit quality.
Credit Products & Structuring
Define the new-deal hand-off from origination to PM, clarifying deal understanding, owners and post-close items.
Support LUs that elect a greater PM role in new-business underwriting; origination retains client ownership and negotiation.
Provide structuring expertise and coaching on complex transactions; evaluate new and tailored financing structures and related policy changes.
Talent & Capability Development
Establish PM competency standards, training curriculum and career frameworks, coordinating with the Training working group.
Lead PM succession planning and talent development; set junior staffing principles that allow flexible deployment across LUs.
PM Effectiveness & Operating Model
Drive process simplification, automation and operating-model enhancements across PM workflows.
Oversee centralized mid-to-back-office support (LC, TPS, KYC), with PM retaining risk decisions and accountability.
Oversee PM KPIs and performance measurements across Corporate Banking, in coordination with the KPI task force.
Continue oversight and management of the BA team.
Leadership & Culture
Promote the Bank’s risk culture: clear accountabilities, open communication, effective challenge and tone from the top.
Lead and mentor a diverse team; develop leaders, plan succession and attract and retain top talent.
Foster an inclusive environment and a high-performance culture; role model One Bank leadership and the Bank’s Ambition.

Qualifications

Post-secondary education or equivalent work experience; CPA or MBA or equivalent experience in finance, accounting and business law.
20+ years in financial services in a corporate lending environment developing business; 10+ years negotiating and structuring financial transactions with expertise in Leveraged Finance.
Credit qualified, with expert knowledge of credit risk management and credit philosophy, policies and procedures.
Working knowledge of U.S. and/or Canadian regulatory expectations; experience leading regulator and Internal Audit engagements.
Command of portfolio management concepts: allowance and provisioning, RWA, return on capital, concentration and limit frameworks.
Expertise across key corporate lending sectors, with in-depth knowledge of corporate banking products and services.
Experience managing a large, diverse team and influencing LU leaders where decision rights are shared.
Highly developed written and oral communication and relationship-building skills.
Expert analytical thinking, change leadership, negotiation and risk management; in-depth strategic business planning.

Le rôle adresse des enjeux structurels récurrents dans l’exécution commerciale, notamment les contrats, l’exposition aux risques, la visibilité sur le funnel, l’efficacité de l’intégration des nouveaux employés et l’adoption de Salesforce. Il amène de la rigueur de processus dans une fonction qui a historiquement reposé davantage sur l’expérience individuelle que sur une discipline institutionnelle. Les opérations commerciales corporatives bâtissent le système pour permettre aux Ventes / Marketing / Légal / Finances / CX de travailler ensemble efficacement.

La fonction corporative d’expérience client relèvera du/de la Directeur(trice), opérations commerciales corporatives, ce qui est un arrimage naturel puisque la Voix du client, l’adoption de Salesforce, la discipline du funnel, la boucle fermée et les cadences commerciales doivent être connectées au même système de gestion pour transformer les commentaires clients en actions concrètes, soutenir la rétention, favoriser la croissance et améliorer l’exécution opérationnelle.

Facteurs de succès dans le rôle

Le succès dans ce rôle sera évalué sur les résultats du système, et non sur le niveau d’activité.

L’exécution des ventes devient reproductible
Moins d’exceptions gérées à la pièce; un flux de dossiers plus constant à travers les mêmes étapes et approbations.

Les leaders des ventes utilisent les outils parce qu’ils les aident à gérer le business
Salesforce est utilisé parce qu’il facilite la gestion commerciale, et non seulement parce qu’il est obligatoire.

Les risques commerciaux sont visibles avant les décisions
Les responsables P&L peuvent voir la durée des contrats, l’exposition aux termes de paiement et les engagements de responsabilité avant d’approuver les ententes.

Moins de surprises
Moins d’escalades de dernière minute causées par des termes non documentés, des approbations floues ou des incohérences entre régions.

Crédibilité accrue du funnel
Les discussions de prévisions sont basées sur une vision partagée et disciplinée du pipeline.

La boucle de rétroaction CX est intégrée au processus de ventes afin d’améliorer les scores CX dans l’ensemble des unités d’affaires.

Portée et responsabilités clés

Ce rôle établit les standards et anime la gouvernance. Les leaders des ventes demeurent propriétaires de l’exécution. Les finances, le crédit et le légal codéfinissent les règles d’approbation et les seuils de risque.

Modèle opérationnel des ventes et gouvernance
Définir et maintenir le modèle opérationnel commercial de première ligne, incluant les flux d’approbation des contrats, les limites d’autorité et les règles applicables aux clients opérant dans plusieurs régions.
Travailler avec le juridique, les finances et le crédit afin de rendre le risque explicite et prêt à être décidé.
S’assurer que les leaders P&L ont la visibilité requise avant que les engagements soient pris, et non après.
Ownership Salesforce
Agir comme propriétaire d’affaires de Salesforce pour le design des processus, les standards d’utilisation et la logique de reporting.
Favoriser l’adoption en définissant clairement comment et pourquoi Salesforce est utilisé.
Aligner la structure du funnel avec les besoins d’affaires, incluant le mix produit, la saisonnalité et la capacité.
Développer des tableaux de bord standards pour les responsables P&L et les leaders des ventes.
Réduire le bruit administratif afin que l’outil soutienne les décisions, plutôt que de devenir une couche de reporting additionnelle.
Gestion du funnel et planification des ventes
Définir et faire vivre des pratiques cohérentes à travers le groupe de gestion du funnel.
Donner une visibilité prospective sur la concentration des revenus par usine, type d’actif, industrie, représentant et autres découpages nécessaires.
Permettre des discussions proactives sur la capacité et la production, plutôt que de fonctionner en mode réaction ou escalade.
Contribuer au développement de plans de ventes clairs, prêts à être transférés en exécution.
Permettre une consolidation au niveau du groupe de ces données.
Contrats, termes et suivi des risques
Mettre en place un reporting standardisé sur la durée des contrats, l’exposition aux termes de paiement et les engagements de responsabilité.
Rendre le risque commercial mesurable, visible et discutable, plutôt qu’implicite ou anecdotique.
Formation, mobilisation et gestion des incitatifs de ventes
Concevoir et institutionnaliser un cadre formel d’intégration et de formation pour les équipes de ventes.
Développer des formations adaptées aux rôles, notamment sur Salesforce et les notions de base liées aux contrats.
Bâtir une cadence reproductible pour les rencontres de ventes afin de renforcer les thèmes clés et l’exécution.

Senior Regional Vice President

Detailed Job Description

Job Overview

The Senior Regional Vice President (SRVP) is responsible for leading and managing overall business operations, market development, strategic execution, and organizational management within a designated region, ensuring that regional operational goals align with the company’s overarching strategic direction. This role entails comprehensive oversight of regional business performance, operational management, financial results, market expansion, client relations, and team development. The SRVP drives sustainable growth within the region while ensuring that all business activities comply with company policies, standards, and management requirements.

The SRVP works closely with the CEO, COO, CFO, other regional leaders, and the corporate executive team to formulate regional development strategies, facilitate cross-regional resource coordination, oversee the execution of major business initiatives, and resolve critical operational issues. Furthermore, the SRVP is responsible for cultivating regional management talent, optimizing operational systems, and enhancing market competitiveness to ensure long-term, stable business growth and operational success within the assigned region.

Key Responsibilities

I. Regional Strategic Planning and Leadership

Develop and implement long-term development strategies and annual operational plans for the assigned region, ensuring that regional objectives are aligned with the company’s overall strategy, financial goals, and market development direction. Analyze the regional market environment, industry trends, competitive landscape, and customer needs to identify new business opportunities and potential risks. Establish regional management standards and execution mechanisms, define the responsibilities, objectives, and performance requirements for each business unit, and drive the effective implementation of regional strategies.

II. Regional Business Operations and Performance Management

Provide comprehensive oversight of the daily operations of all business departments, branches, and operational units within the region, ensuring that business processes run efficiently and meet established performance targets. Regularly review revenue performance, operational efficiency, service quality, customer satisfaction, and business growth; identify operational deviations promptly and develop corrective measures. Coordinate activities across different departments within the region to resolve significant issues that impact business execution and operational efficiency.

III. Financial Management and Operational Goal Control

Oversee regional budget development, financial planning, cost control, and the analysis of operational results, ensuring that regional financial objectives align with the company’s overall financial plan. Collaborate with the CFO and the finance team to review regional revenue, profit, operating expenses, cash flow, and return on investment (ROI). Establish mechanisms for monitoring budget execution and financial performance; control operating costs effectively; enhance the efficiency of regional resource utilization; and ensure that all business units achieve their established financial objectives.

IV. Market Expansion and Business Growth

Lead regional market development, business expansion, and commercial growth initiatives, identifying potential customer segments, emerging markets, and strategic partnership opportunities. Oversee the development of sales channels, customer acquisition, marketing campaigns, and business collaborations to drive the growth of regional market share and enhance corporate brand influence. Partner with business development, sales, and marketing teams to formulate market-entry strategies and customer growth plans, ensuring the sustained competitiveness of the regional business.

V. Organizational Management and Team Leadership

Responsible for establishing and refining the regional management structure, and overseeing the performance of regional department heads and senior management. Define team performance objectives, talent development programs, and succession plans for management roles to strengthen regional organizational capabilities and the execution proficiency of the leadership team. Foster a positive corporate culture and cross-departmental collaboration, ensuring that managers at all levels effectively implement company policies, operational goals, and management requirements.

VI. Customer Relations and Strategic Partnership Management

Oversee the management of key regional customer relationships, strategic partnerships, and major commercial contracts, ensuring timely responses to customer needs and the stability of collaborative ties. Participate in negotiations with major clients, business collaborations, and the drafting and review of critical business agreements; coordinate the resolution of significant customer complaints, service disputes, and partnership-related issues. Collaborate with customer success, sales, and operations teams to improve customer satisfaction, retention rates, and long-term partnership value.

VII. Risk Management and Compliance Oversight

Monitor operational, financial, legal, and market risks within regional business activities, and establish effective mechanisms for risk identification, assessment, and mitigation. Ensure that all regional business units comply with applicable laws, industry regulations, internal corporate policies, and regulatory requirements. Work with legal, compliance, finance, and internal audit teams to periodically review regional management processes and internal controls, addressing significant compliance issues promptly and driving the implementation of corrective actions.

VIII. Communication with Senior Management and Strategic Execution

Provide regular reports to the CEO, COO, and the corporate executive management team regarding regional operational performance, market developments, financial results, business risks, and the progress of strategic plan execution. Provide management counsel regarding regional expansion, organizational restructuring, major investments, and business transformation. Facilitate the sharing of resources and information between various regions and corporate headquarters, ensure the unified execution of corporate strategy at the regional level, and drive long-term, sustainable growth for regional operations.

Qualifications

Education

Bachelor’s degree or higher in Business Administration, Management, Marketing, Financial Management, Economics, or a related field.

A Master of Business Administration (MBA) or a postgraduate degree in a relevant field is preferred.

Prior training in areas such as corporate operations management, strategic planning, financial management, or leadership is an advantage.

Proficiency in corporate management, regional market strategy, budget management, and risk control principles.

Work Experience

At least 20 years of professional experience in corporate management, business operations, market expansion, or regional management.

At least 7 years of experience in senior management or regional leadership roles.

Proven, hands-on experience in managing multiple business units, branches, or cross-regional operational teams.

A successful track record in developing regional business strategies, managing budgets, driving business growth, and enhancing operational performance.

Experience in managing cross-regional operations, or working within large-scale or multinational corporate environments, is preferred.

Who is Mastercard?

Mastercard is a global technology company in the payments industry. Our mission is to connect and power an inclusive, digital economy that benefits everyone, everywhere by making transactions safe, simple, smart, and accessible. Using secure data and networks, partnerships and passion, our innovations and solutions help individuals, financial institutions, governments, and businesses realize their greatest potential.

Our decency quotient, or DQ, drives our culture and everything we do inside and outside of our company. With connections across more than 210 countries and territories, we are building a sustainable world that unlocks priceless possibilities for all.

Overview

Small and medium enterprises are the backbone of the Canadian economy. They represent more than 98% of businesses, contribute approximately 35% of Canada's GDP, and employ over half of the country's workforce. Behind these numbers are millions of entrepreneurs and business owners pursuing their ambitions, investing in growth, and shaping the future of their communities. Mastercard is committed to helping businesses move from aspiration to achievement by providing the products, partnerships, insights, and capabilities they need to grow and thrive. This segment is central to Mastercard's growth strategy, not only because of its economic impact, but also because SMEs play a vital role in the payments ecosystem as both buyers and sellers of digital payment solutions.

The Canadian Small & Medium Enterprises team is looking for a Director, Product Management to help drive our growth in the segment through solution innovation & commercialization, value proposition enhancements (core & via partnerships), distribution of Mastercard products and solutions via channel distribution channels, and P&L optimization. The ideal candidate is passionate about the Small & Medium Enterprises segment, highly motivated, intellectually curious, analytical, and possesses an entrepreneurial mindset.

Role

In This Product Management Position The Selected Candidate Will

Execute against our strategy to capture incremental segment share and help secure market, divisional leadership

Analyze market trends, competition, and SME lifecycle journeys to inform product and go-to-market strategies, driving product differentiation and innovation 

Identify partnership opportunities to drive value proposition improvements and new distribution channels

Support and/or Lead the implementation of new product development initiatives, Product Line Strategy execution, and portfolio optimization activities in collaboration with Services

Collaborate with cross functional stakeholders (e.g. O&T, Finance, Legal, Marketing, Market Development, Account Management, Services, etc.) to deliver on role and business objectives (eg. portfolio growth, financial analysis/P&L driver optimization, marketing & sales materials, product enhancements, etc.) 

Support business development and account management colleagues in customer-facing discussions to help advance SME objectives

Collaborate with the broader Commercial & New Payment Flows team to help design and execute relevant use cases to advance digital solutions for the segment

Work with other regional and divisional teams ensure sales readiness and training by developing necessary sales enablement tools for SMEs

All About You

Be passionate about ‘empowering every business everywhere’ and the idea of democratizing access to powerful tools that help SMEs thrive 

Have proven experience in engaging internal and external commercial and technical stakeholders to drive both solution development and adoption

Have intermediate experience in financial services and/or payments with an understanding of competitive offerings, industry trends and profitability drivers

SME banking or SME payment experience, international market knowledge/experience a plus

Have a keen understanding of competitive offerings, industry trends and go-to-market considerations; ability to translate that understanding into meaningful action and enhancements 

Have demonstrated ability to work across divisional and regional boundaries; strong relationship management, influencing, presentation/verbal and communication skills

Be self-motivated, a self-starter and a quick learner with ability to work independently and manage different priorities; thrives in a fast-paced environment; readiness to take-on stretch goals
